title: TNS: Fix two length misreads in the TTI_OER decoder
description:
A follow-up to !26411, which added the TTI_OER decoding. Re-checking it
against the same reference the series was written from turned up two
places where a byte was treated as a length when it isn't one. Two
commits, one per case, each with the fixture frame that demonstrates it.

### The DALC null marker

A DALC's leading byte is a length only in the middle of its range:
`0x00` is empty, `0xFE` opens the chunked form, and `0xFF` is a null
marker that stands for itself with no data behind it. The decoder
handled the first two and let `0xFF` fall through to the plain-length
branch, where it claims 255 bytes that aren't there — every field after
it lands at the wrong offset, and near the end of a packet the read runs
off the frame and the whole thing is reported as malformed.

### bytes_with_length

A `bytes_with_length` / `str_with_length` field is a ub4 count followed
by a DALC, and the DALC is present only when the count is non-zero. The
decoder read `oerrdd` and the batch-error message entries as a bare
DALC.

An empty field is the count alone — a single zero byte — which a bare
DALC read also consumes in one byte, so the two agree on every capture
where the field is empty. That's every capture one normally sees, which
is why this went unnoticed. As soon as the field carries something, the
count byte is mistaken for a length and the rest of the block decodes
one field early: on a real error the ORA-NNNNN message quietly
disappears.

The batch error-code and offset arrays get the same treatment from the
other side — each is a count and then one DALC packing that many ub4
values, not a byte to skip followed by the values inline. Both readings
consume the same bytes while the packed values fit a short DALC, but
only one keeps working when the array grows past that.

### Not reachable in ordinary traffic

Neither case appears in any capture I have, which is why the existing
tests pass on the unfixed code. Both need a server to fill in a field
that is normally empty — a logical rowid in `oerrdd`, or a null rather
than empty message. Nothing here is in a released branch, so there's no
backport to consider.

### Testing

`test/captures/tns_oer.pcap` grows from two frames to four, one per
case, and each commit was checked against its own parent: without the
first fix the null-marker frame is reported as `[Malformed Packet]`;
without the second the `oerrdd` frame silently loses its ORA-00942
message text.

Its generator also had to start advancing the TCP sequence number by the
bytes actually sent. Numbering the segments 1, 2, 3 was harmless with
two frames, but the third then overlaps the second and is read as a
retransmission rather than dissected.

Both commits build individually with `-Werror`; at the tip the TNS tests
pass, clang-tidy is clean, and the fixtures regenerate byte-identically.

### Not changed

The chunk lengths inside the `0xFE` form are single bytes here. That's
the 11g shape this dissector decodes throughout — 12.2 and later prefix
each chunk with a variable-length ub4 instead, and telling the two apart
needs the field version negotiated during the handshake, which isn't
threaded through the dissector. Left alone, with a comment recording it
so it isn't "fixed" in the wrong direction.

-"""Generate test/captures/tns_oer.pcap with two TTI_OER frames:

+    Frame 4 — failure with a non-empty oerrdd, so that field is a ub4 count
+                                followed by a DALC rather than a bare DALC
 
 Bytes are constructed by hand in the Oracle 11g wire shape.
 """
@@ -46,8 +50,16 @@ def dalc(s: bytes | None) -> bytes:
     return out
 
 
+def bytes_with_length(s: bytes | None) -> bytes:
+    """A ub4 count, and a DALC carrying the value only when it is non-empty."""
+    if not s:
+        return ub4(0)
+    return ub4(len(s)) + dalc(s)
+
+
 def build_oer(call_status: int, rowcount: int, err_code: int, cursor_id: int,
-              message: bytes | None) -> bytes:
+              message: bytes | None, message_raw: bytes | None = None,
+              oerrdd: bytes | None = None) -> bytes:
     b = b"\x04"                       # TTI_OER token
     b += ub4(call_status)
     b += ub4(0)                       # end-to-end seq#
@@ -68,12 +80,12 @@ def build_oer(call_status: int, rowcount: int, err_code: int, cursor_id: int,
     b += b"\x00\x00"                  # statement #, call #
     b += ub4(0)                       # padding (ub2 in 11g)
     b += ub4(1)                       # successful iterations
-    b += dalc(None)                   # oerrdd (logical rowid)
+    b += bytes_with_length(oerrdd)    # oerrdd (logical rowid)
     b += ub4(0)                       # num batch errcodes
     b += ub4(0)                       # num batch offsets
     b += ub4(0)                       # num batch messages
     if err_code != 0:
-        b += dalc(message or b"")
+        b += message_raw if message_raw is not None else dalc(message or b"")
     return b
 
 
@@ -81,6 +93,15 @@ frames = [
     build_oer(call_status=0, rowcount=3, err_code=0, cursor_id=42, message=None),
     build_oer(call_status=0, rowcount=0, err_code=1, cursor_id=42,
               message=b"ORA-00001: unique constraint (TEST.PK) violated\n"),
+    # A null message. 0xFF is a marker, not a length of 255 - reading it as
+    # one walks off the end of the frame.
+    build_oer(call_status=0, rowcount=0, err_code=1722, cursor_id=9,
+              message=None, message_raw=b"\xff"),
+    # A logical rowid in oerrdd. Read as a bare DALC the count byte is taken
+    # for a length, and every field after it lands one field early.
+    build_oer(call_status=0, rowcount=0, err_code=942, cursor_id=7,
+              message=b"ORA-00942: table or view does not exist\n",
+              oerrdd=b"\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07\x08"),
 ]
 
 
@@ -102,7 +123,7 @@ def tcp_checksum(src: bytes, dst: bytes, seg: bytes) -> int:
     return (~s) & 0xFFFF
 
 
-def wrap(body: bytes, seq: int) -> bytes:
+def wrap(body: bytes, seq: int, ident: int) -> bytes:
     # TNS DATA framing (10 bytes).
     tns = struct.pack(">HhBBhh", len(body) + 10, 0, 6, 0, 0, 0) + body
 
@@ -120,7 +141,7 @@ def wrap(body: bytes, seq: int) -> bytes:
     seg = tcp + tns
 
     ip_total = 20 + len(seg)
-    ip_no = struct.pack(">BBHHHBBH", 0x45, 0, ip_total, seq, 0x4000, 64, 6, 0) + src_ip + dst_ip
+    ip_no = struct.pack(">BBHHHBBH", 0x45, 0, ip_total, ident, 0x4000, 64, 6, 0) + src_ip + dst_ip
     ip = ip_no[:10] + struct.pack(">H", ipv4_checksum(ip_no)) + ip_no[12:]
     return ip + seg
 
@@ -128,8 +149,12 @@ def wrap(body: bytes, seq: int) -> bytes:
 out = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "tns_oer.pcap")
 with open(out, "wb") as f:
     f.write(struct.pack("<IHHIIII", 0xA1B2C3D4, 2, 4, 0, 0, 65535, 101))
+    # Sequence numbers have to advance by the bytes actually sent, or TCP

commits_data.title: TNS: Read a bytes_with_length as a count and a value
commits_data.message:
TNS: Read a bytes_with_length as a count and a value

A bytes_with_length / str_with_length field is a ub4 count followed
by a DALC, and the DALC is there only when the count is non-zero.
The OER decoder read the oerrdd and the batch-error message entries
as a bare DALC instead.

An empty field is the count alone — a single zero byte — which a
bare DALC read also consumes in one byte, so the two agree on every
capture where the field is empty. That is every capture anyone
normally sees, which is why this went unnoticed. As soon as the
field carries something the count byte is mistaken for a length,
the value's own length byte is mistaken for the next field, and the
rest of the block decodes one field early: on a real error the
ORA-NNNNN message quietly disappears.

Add get_field_with_length for the shape and use it in both places.

The batch error-code and offset arrays get the same treatment from
the other side: each is a count and then one DALC packing that many
ub4 values, not a byte to skip followed by the values inline. Both
readings consume the same bytes while the packed values fit a short
DALC, but only one keeps working when the array grows past that.

The fixture gains a fourth frame carrying a logical rowid in
oerrdd, which loses its ORA-00942 message text without this.

commits_data.title: TNS: Read the DALC null marker as a marker
commits_data.message:
TNS: Read the DALC null marker as a marker

A DALC's leading byte is a length only in the middle of its range.
0x00 is empty, 0xFE opens the chunked form, and 0xFF is a null
marker that stands for itself with no data behind it. The decoder
handled the first two and let 0xFF fall through to the plain
length branch, where it claims 255 bytes that are not there: every
field after it lands at the wrong offset, and near the end of a
packet the read runs off the frame and the whole thing is reported
as malformed.

Give the marker its own branch, consuming just itself. Spelling it
out next to the empty case also documents the range, so the next
reader doesn't have to infer which byte values are lengths.

While here, record what the chunk lengths in the 0xFE form are:
single bytes, the 11g shape decoded throughout this dissector.
12.2 and later prefix each chunk with a variable-length ub4
instead, and telling the two apart needs the field version
negotiated during the handshake, which isn't threaded through yet.

The fixture gains a third frame whose message is the null marker,
which is reported as a malformed packet without the fix. Its
generator also had to start advancing the TCP sequence number by
the bytes actually sent — numbering the segments 1, 2, 3 was
harmless while there were two, but the third frame then overlaps
the second and is read as a retransmission rather than dissected.

Assisted-by: Claude
Signed-off-by: Peter Lemenkov <lemenkov@gmail.com>
